newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU must take care of its people to work - Santer.
newsitem.headline: EU must take care of its people to work - Santer.

text.p: The European Union must change its ways and focus more clearly on the aspirations of its people if it wants their support, European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Wednesday.

"Our joint project...has to reflect the feelings and aspirations of our citizens," Santer told the European Parliament EU assembly during a ceremony to mark the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome.
The Treaty founded the EU's ancestor, the European Economic Community.
The initial aim of the "European project" -- to solve national differences peacefully and find common answers to European people's needs -- remained as valid in 1997 as it was in 1957, Santer said.
But the EU needed to ask itself some searching questions about the way it was going about this task.

It had concentrated on economic cooperation but in its haste to create a single market it had left other, vital concerns by the wayside, "with dramatic implications at times", Santer told the EU assembly.

People would not back the Union if it did not also tackle unemployment and give them proper social and health protection, he added, speaking a day after thousands of European car workers protested in Paris against plans by carmaker Renault to close an assembly plant in Belgium, with the loss of 3,000 jobs.

The EU had succeeded in abolishing national borders for criminals but not for national police forces, Santer continued. It had a common trade policy but hadn't been able to reap political benefits from it.
The former Luxembourg prime minister said EU governments needed to tackle all these problems during their ongoing reform of the EU treaty.
Even Jean Monnet, one of Europe's founding fathers, had been aware 40 years ago that common institutions should be a means of bringing people together, not an end in themselves, Santer said.
"We have to make Europe a Europe of our people," he said.
